title: What LOADS+RUNS a content class's .lpb (defines it / +0x7d=1) and what triggers it for the OpeningDirector: the loader is Lua-require-driven only; the director class is never require()d during the bahamut opening
trigger: docs/director-class-load-handoff.md (follow-up to client-architecture 'Zone-in actor bind and Lua-class-readiness pipeline': what loads+runs the OpeningDirector .prog?)

Q1_lazy_on_resolve.verdict: NO. Resolve uses FUN_00CD8870(name, create=0) - it does not load. Class definition is eager-via-Lua-require, not lazy-on-resolve.

Q2_what_triggers_the_load.verdict: A Lua `require(name)` call from a running script. The loader chain FUN_00D08A10 (_luaGameEngineRequire) -> FUN_00D0CFB0 (file lookup) -> FUN_00D08180 (_luaGameEngineLoad) -> FUN_00CF4680 (luaL_loadbuffer) runs the .lpb, whose top-level _defineClass reaches FUN_00CD9360 -> FUN_00CE1DD0 -> +0x7d=1. FUN_00D08A10 has ONLY a DATA xref (registered as a Lua C fn by FUN_00CD8990) - so the loader is invoked solely via Lua require() dispatch; there is NO native/server 'load class X' trigger. The server influences it only by driving the Lua flow (opening/content script) that issues the require.

Q3_player_vs_director.verdict: The player/chara/world classes are require()d by the core login/world bootstrap (always run). The director (OpeningDirector) is a CONTENT class, require()d only when the opening/content flow runs.

Q4_what_bahamut_must_send.verdict: Drive the client's opening sequence / content-instance flow so its Lua require()s + _createActor()s the director - NOT just AddActor + ActorInstantiate. The director class load is a SIDE EFFECT of running the opening script. Ensure the parent DirectorBaseClass loads too.
Q4_what_bahamut_must_send.differentiator: ActorInstantiate is sent for the PLAYER too (player_spawn.cpp:188; test 'starter-city self spawn ActorInstantiate should bind the player script') AND the director (director_spawn.cpp:374). Player class is DEFINED (works); director class is not. So ActorInstantiate only BINDS actor->class-name (control + tentative ref); it does not load the class.

directorsArePureLua: zero EXE functions named Director/Judge. A director is an Actor created via the global Lua binding _createActor(className,...) which dispatches vtable[0x6c] and REQUIRES the class already defined (finding_createActor_thunk_async_actor_factory.md). FUN_00758260 (decompiled) is the DirectorBaseClass NATIVE method-surface master (5 registrars), NOT the Lua class definition.
functionsExamined: FUN_00D0CFB0 (BCS-Y-1811 NEW) - LpbLoader file lookup; path+.lpb retry; not-found -> return 2
FUN_00CD8990 (BCS-Y-1813 NEW) - boot registrar; binds require/load; seeds 5 category tags d4f8..d508; loads boot chunk
FUN_00758260 - DirectorBaseClass native master (5 registrars; method surface, NOT the Lua class def) - ruled out
FUN_00CD9360 (BCS-Y-1806, amended) - class-define registrar; runs when a .lpb is loaded by the chain
runtimeNextSteps: Frida (entry hooks only): FUN_00D08A10 (0x00D08A10; capture require'd filename) + FUN_00D0CFB0 (0x00D0CFB0; name + found/notfound) + FUN_00CD9360 (0x00CD9360; names DEFINED). Director name never reaching D08A10/0CFB0 => require never issued (case a); reaching 0CFB0 but return 2 => path/version (case b).

bahamut: drive the opening event/content-instance flow that retail uses for the new-character opening, so the client require()s + creates the OpeningDirector + DirectorBaseClass; compare against a working opening capture for the trigger packet/sequence.
